status.transport: parent-created Linux anonymous memfd, MAP_SHARED, exactly 4 bytes
status.parent_lifetime: Initialize the mapping to zero and seal its size before launch. Pass the descriptor through pass_fds and retain the mapping until the actual renderer process has exited.
status.native_lifetime: Strictly parse the decimal descriptor, fstat size 4 and mmap before trace-file creation. Keep the shared mapping for process lifetime. No per-event allocation.
status.transitions: Store active only after successful session_start. Set clean only after successful session_end with an atomic active-to-clean compare/exchange. Every logging failure and every late event stores failed. Failed never returns to clean.
status.acceptance: Read status only after actual process death. Complete capture requires clean status 2 AND valid complete JSONL. Zero, active, failed, missing status or setup/read failure means incomplete capture, even if JSONL ends with a clean footer.

semantics.ordering: Sequence starts at 1 per process. The logger assigns sequence and CLOCK_MONOTONIC time under one mutex. Map observations occur under the existing color-buffer-map lock.
semantics.generation: Each successful register starts a new handle generation. Erase means logical map removal, not final C++ object destruction. Requests without a map observation do not establish a generation.
semantics.references: Present events have found=true and a uint32 refcount. Observed events have boolean found and numeric refcount exactly when found. Requests and session/loss events have null refcount/found.
semantics.erase: Erase records precede the protected native erase/clear statement. No erased iterator is read. A terminated process can lack a completed removal; require a clean complete session before drawing lifecycle conclusions.
semantics.completion: A valid complete capture requires parent-observed shared status 2 after actual renderer death, plus session_start, final session_end, contiguous sequence and no loss. No JSONL footer alone proves completion.
semantics.failure: Either bound emits loss(limit) when possible and stores shared failed status 3. Clock, formatting, write, mutex, atexit or trace-file initialization failure also stores failed status. Missing or invalid status mapping leaves parent status 0 and prevents trace-file creation. A late event stores failed BEFORE attempting loss(late_event), so a zero-byte failed append cannot preserve completion. Partial metadata remains readable; no arbitrary error text is emitted.
semantics.process: The file is exclusively created with mode 0600 and O_NOFOLLOW. A fork child never writes the parent session. A restart cannot overwrite an existing file. Use a fresh private absolute file path for every emulator invocation.
semantics.privacy: Records contain fixed enums and numeric lifecycle metadata only. No pixels, guest data, commands, credentials, addresses, or free-form strings.
